correctness.rationale: The support bound follows from a tail-preimage contraction argument and requires no moment assumption. Invariance plus the pointwise identity |F(z)-c|=u|z| gives equality of the complete radial pushforward laws. The second moment completes to an exact circle centered at c/(1-u^2), and bias–variance gives the mean disk. Boundary equality forces zero variance and hence a fixed-point atom; conversely every fixed-point atom lies on the Apollonius boundary. The checker verifies the core rotation-norm identity and standard rational specialization.

value.rationale: The Ikeda map is a canonical optical chaos model with well-developed horseshoe, generating-partition, and invariant-measure approximation literature. The result gives a distribution-level calibration independent of the nonlinear phase: every radial CDF/quantile about the pump is an exact scaled copy of the origin-centered radial law. The sharp mean–variance disk supplies a low-dimensional diagnostic for sampled invariant measures and cleanly separates fixed-point atoms from every genuinely fluctuating invariant state. At u=0.9 it gives exact rational center/radius values and an automatic support bound, making the statement directly reusable rather than an arbitrary isolated moment computation.
